commands.name: tunnel
commands.about: Share a running site on the internet through a tunnel (Cloudflare Quick Tunnels)
notes: LocDev runs the provider's own program; it never relays traffic itself. Only the site's own server is shared (never the proxy, a database or LocDev), with the site's domain as Host.

commands.about: Download and verify a provider's program (cloudflare)
notes: Downloads cloudflared from Cloudflare's GitHub release only when the checksum in the release notes and the one GitHub reports for the file agree, and checks the download against it. A cloudflared already on PATH (Homebrew, apt) is used as is.

args.help: Only these e-mail addresses (or *@domain) may open it; repeatable or comma-separated

args.name: -y, --yes
args.help: Don't ask before exposing the site

notes: The site must be running. The address (https://….trycloudflare.com) changes every time and stops working when the tunnel stops; up to 200 requests at the same time, no Server-Sent Events. With --allow, visitors confirm their e-mail with a one-time PIN.

notes: `locdev new <starter> <name>` is the same as `locdev new project <starter> <name>` and takes the same options; alone, in a terminal, `locdev new` asks what to create.

commands.name: new project
commands.about: A new project, created with the framework's own installer (the plan is shown first)

args.name: <starter>
args.help: The starter (`locdev new list`): laravel, symfony, php, wordpress, bedrock, nextjs, vite, vue, angular, nuxt, astro, sveltekit, nestjs, django, flask, fastapi, rust, rails, dotnet

args.help: Folder (and site) name: lowercase letters, digits, - and _

args.help: How to create it (installer, composer, npm, pnpm, bun…); the first one by default

args.name: --typescript
args.help: TypeScript, for starters that offer it (same as `-o language=ts`)

args.name: --php
args.help: PHP version to create it with and pin the site to (8.4)

args.help: Node.js version to create it with and pin the site to (22)

args.name: -o, --option
args.help: A starter option, KEY=VALUE (see `locdev new list`). Repeatable

args.name: -p, --package
args.help: A package to add after creating it (npm or Composer, by the starter). Repeatable

args.name: --database
args.help: A LocDev database for it, SERVICE:INSTANCE (postgres:db, mysql:main…); the instance is created if needed

args.name: --in
args.help: The folder to create it in (the current one by default)

args.name: --no-site
args.help: Don't register it as a site at the end

args.name: -y, --yes
args.help: Run without asking (still shows the plan)

examples: locdev new project laravel shop -o kit=react --database postgres:db
locdev new project nextjs web --method pnpm -o linter=biome -p zod
notes: Runs the framework's own installer (laravel new, composer create-project, npm create vite, create-vue, ng new, rails new, cargo init…) without a shell, after showing every command. Output streams here and what you type goes to the installer. The folder must not exist. At the end the folder is registered as a site; with --database, the instance and database are created and the new project's .env points at them.

Plain PHP, Flask, FastAPI and the Rust servers have no generator: LocDev writes its own minimal files (shown in the plan) into the new folder first, then pip or Cargo runs. --php/--node pick the version the installer runs with, and the new site is pinned to it.

commands.details:
Make a site HTTPS-only, checking and fixing what that needs.

Checks DNS, the HTTPS listener, the site's certificate and whether the LocDev CA is trusted. Changes that need administrator rights (trusting the CA, routing *.test) are shown and confirmed first.

Firefox and Chrome on Linux keep their own certificate store; it is updated as your user.

commands.details:
Append the shared variables a site is missing to one of its .env files.

Without a site, every registered site. Only adds lines, after showing them; keeps a backup; never copies secrets into .env.production or .env.staging, and writes .env.example with empty placeholders.

args.help: Target file (default .env)

args.name: --dry-run
args.help: Show what would change and stop

args.name: -y, --yes
args.help: Do not ask before writing

notes: Without a site, every registered site.
Only appends lines; comments, order, encoding and line endings stay as they were. An encrypted backup is taken first (`locdev env backups`).
Secrets never go into .env.production or .env.staging; .env.example gets empty placeholders.

commands.name: actions
commands.about: GitHub Actions workflows: templates, checks, new files

commands.about: Templates that fit the site, and its workflow files

commands.name: actions new
commands.about: A workflow from a template, printed (or saved with --save)

args.name: --file
args.help: File name under .github/workflows/ (the template's by default)

args.name: --save
args.help: Write it, after showing the file and the checks. Never replaces a file

args.name: -y, --yes
args.help: Do not ask before saving

notes: Prints the workflow and its checks. --save creates the file after asking, and never replaces one: edit existing files in the app, which shows the diff.

commands.name: actions validate
commands.about: Check the site's workflow files (or one of them, or any YAML file)

args.name: --file
args.help: Only this file (e.g. ci.yml)

args.name: --yaml
args.help: Check a YAML file from disk instead (`-` for stdin); no site needed

notes: Structure, script injection, pull_request_target, token permissions, unpinned and outdated actions; actionlint too when it is on PATH. Exits with 1 when there are errors.

commands.name: actions save
commands.about: Write a workflow you edited as .github/workflows/<file>: the diff and the checks first; an existing file is replaced only as it was reviewed

args.name: <file>
args.help: File name under .github/workflows/ (e.g. ci.yml)

args.name: --from
args.help: The YAML to write (`-` for stdin)

commands.name: actions versions
commands.about: The action versions templates use; --refresh asks GitHub

commands.name: actions history
commands.about: Local versions LocDev kept of a workflow file; --show prints one

args.name: <file>
args.help: File name under .github/workflows/ (e.g. ci.yml)

args.name: --show
args.help: A version id from the list

notes: LocDev keeps a version when it reads a workflow changed outside it and around every save (50 per file).

commands.name: actions install-actionlint
commands.about: Download actionlint (verified) so validation uses it
notes: From rhysd/actionlint's latest GitHub release; installed only when the release's checksums file and GitHub's digest agree on the SHA-256.
